# Facilities Desk Access Addendum

Fictional evaluation document. Scope: access administration for the 2027 policy year. Effective dates are supplied separately in the corpus manifest. This document must be read alongside other selected sources when the question names another office or location.

## Key deposit

The facilities desk addendum lists a refundable temporary key deposit of AUD 35.

Building entry arrangements do not waive supervision rules inside teaching spaces. Staff establish which location and document the visitor is asking about before giving instructions. An accessibility request is not a request for a diagnosis. For this section the desk records the request under ACCESS-2027-01. The reference groups correspondence; it does not change the deadline or amount stated above. A correction must preserve the original entry and record the reason for the change.

## Working example: key deposit

Consider a case where a visitor arrives before the front desk is staffed. The immediate question concerns key deposit, not every rule in the access file. The administrator checks access logs, room identifiers, and key-return receipts before replying. A common error is that a temporary key deposit is confused with a costume deposit. Read the named source and policy year before treating a nearby number as the answer. Record which document supported the explanation so that another staff member can reproduce the check. ## Cross-service boundary

This access document does not grant authority over unrelated activities. A staff member should distinguish the stated rule from a future booking, payment, or discretionary approval. A family may ask several questions in one message; answerable portions should cite the relevant source while missing facts remain unresolved. An unanswered detail must not be inferred from an adjacent fee, deadline, room number, or event identifier. In particular, general guidance about access logs, room identifiers, and key-return receipts is not a substitute for an explicit rule about a different programme.

## Handling incomplete requests

When a access request omits the student, location, policy year, or relevant date, the desk records the missing information and asks for it. The original wording is preserved in the working notes. Staff avoid copying identity documents into teaching chat or broad distribution lists. A later clarification supplements rather than overwrites the request. This distinction matters when a visitor arrives before the front desk is staffed. A response acknowledging receipt is administrative correspondence and should not be represented as approval of an exception.

## Audit example and non-equivalence

The reviewer reconstructs the event from access logs, room identifiers, and key-return receipts. For example, an entered reference code may identify correspondence without proving that money moved, a class place was reserved, or a consent decision changed. The reviewer compares the dated source with the actual record and records unresolved inconsistencies. Similar words across offices are not proof of identical policies: deposit, credit, submission, and acknowledgement each have a specific role in their own service. The desk retains source identity rather than combining conflicting numbers into a new undocumented rule.

## Final security entry

The facilities desk final security entry records the actual departure time, even if it falls after the scheduled closing time.

This is the last substantive instruction in this source. The closing check must be performed after the ordinary service tasks, not inferred from an earlier example.
